key_insight: A deep reinforcement learning controller trained in a digital twin maintained prescribed indoor comfort limits after deployment in an occupied home without online fine-tuning.
engineering_relevance: The study demonstrates a practical route to coordinating heat pump supply temperature and underfloor heating valves despite slow thermal dynamics.
method: Compare DRL algorithms, control strategies, and configurations in simulation.
Develop a residential building digital twin and train control agents.
Deploy the best-performing agent in the physical building without online fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: Simulation studies and real-building deployment support comfort maintenance, but the abstract reports no quantitative energy savings or evaluation duration.
watch_item: Transfer to other buildings may require new digital twins and validation of robustness under different operating conditions.
paper_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Heat Pump and Underfloor Heating Control: An End-to-End Case Study
